chapter: Musicians and ragtime bands of the time
title: Al Nunez, fakers versus readers, and trombonist Bill Gallaty
summary: He describes Al C. Nunez joining the police band, contrasts natural fakers with legitimate readers, and praises Bill Gallaty as the best ragtime trombone player he ever heard, with tricks like fixing his slide with a hairpin.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yellow, you see his name was Al C. Nunez. We call him Yellow. Al C. Nunez. He was up north for about 15 years. And he came down here and got on the police force. More to get in the band, you know. To have him in the band, he went to the police force, you know. Yes. And he died here. And the other was a very good, wonderful faker. You see, in the days we had clarinet players. We had trombone players. But they could read. But they couldn't fake. You understand? See? They couldn't, they still, you know, other words that they called legitimate music. See? Play as is. Yeah. No improvising and nothing. But these boys had such an ear and they had rhythm. Now there's another one. I don't know if you heard of them. He was one of those. The best ball trombone player, ragtime trombone player, I think in the, that I've never heard no one play like him. Bill Gallaty. You don't want to have heard him talk about. What about? Bill Gallaty.
I've seen his picture and his son plays trombone.

His son plays trombone. Bill would take a trombone and tell you what he wouldn't do with that trombone. He'd take, when his vows wouldn't work, he'd take a hairpin and make a sprinkle. That's a son. He was a little bit of a fuck. He'd pump that thing, I'm telling you, man, just like a swat. Bill Gallaty. At that time, I'll tell you how many white bands, ragtime bands they had here. We had Christian. Frank Christian's band. You heard of him?
